amenitiesDescription: Seaway North residents enjoy the full Four Seasons Surf Club amenity ecosystem: Thomas Keller's restaurant and the adjacent Champagne Bar in the restored historic ballroom, the oceanfront Four Seasons Spa, four pools (including a residents-only pool surrounded by private beachfront gardens), historic beach cabanas originally built in the Prohibition era and beautifully restored, Winston's on the Beach, a state-of-the-art fitness center, and the private members' club. Peter Wirtz's tropical gardens — designed by the firm behind the Tuileries at the Louvre — connect Seaway North to The Surf Club via landscaped pathways. Four Seasons concierge, housekeeping, in-residence dining, and spa services are available on demand.
architectQuote: This is a collectible piece of architecture, designed without constraints.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Seaway North is the rarest format in the rarest location: ten Four Seasons–managed oceanfront homes on the same campus where Seaway South set the county's $86 million record. Trade reporting now describes a completed sellout at 9165 Collins — aggregate consideration cited above $386 million (~$38.6M average × 10), final trade near $41 million — validating the boutique thesis in headline terms. The architecture and service stack mirror Seaway South, but with ten owners instead of thirty-four, structural scarcity is still extreme. For new inventory, the window is closed; for capital, the bet is post-delivery performance in one of the tightest floats on Collins.

investmentThesis: All sponsor residences are sold. Trade reporting (TradedMiami) described Fort Partners closing the final condominium at 9165 Collins Avenue — Surfside's Seaway at The Surf Club North — with aggregate sellout cited above $386 million, a final sale near $41 million, and about $38.6 million average across ten residences ($386 million ÷ 10). That headline sits alongside the adjacent Seaway South, which holds Miami-Dade's all-time condo record at $86 million (November 2025), reinforcing the corridor's pricing power. With only ten homes in the building, ownership float is minimal; the open question is no longer availability but delivery into Four Seasons–managed operations (early 2026), secondary-market liquidity, and how this inventory trades against the rest of The Surf Club campus.
name: Seaway North at The Surf Club
residenceContent:
Seaway North is an 11-story building of ten ultra-luxury residences on a 1-acre Surfside oceanfront site, designed by Joseph Dirand in the same material language as its record-setting sister tower. Seven full-floor tower residences offer uninterrupted flow-through views from Biscayne Bay to the Atlantic Ocean. A two-story beach villa on the ground floors provides direct-access-to-sand living on The Surf Club campus. The penthouse crowns the 10th floor with panoramic exposures in every direction — with further curated homes completing the ten-residence boutique lineup.

Dirand has carried forward the design vocabulary that defined Seaway South — Perla stone terraces that read as if carved from the beach itself, wood-paneled interiors recalling classic yacht staterooms, champagne-colored window frames, and brass hardware throughout. Dedicated elevator landings for the tower homes. No shared walls between residences. The closest thing to single-family oceanfront living inside a Four Seasons-managed building.
tagline: Ten residences. Fully sold at The Surf Club.
